english: Where are you driving the cows? -- It is growing dark. I am driving them to the village. She-wolves come at night. -- Shall I lead the sheep? -- Lead them. Now we eat.
uncertain: h1regwesyeti read as denominative 'grows dark' from h1regwos 'darkness'
h2owins wedhoh2 read as subjunctive question 'shall I lead'

english: What is an otter? -- The otter is a water beast. It lives in the water and swims. -- Have you seen an otter? -- I saw one by the river. My daughter laughed.
uncertain: udros taken as adjective 'watery' agreeing with ghwer
deh2newi h2enti read as 'by/at the river'

english: The cold is great here today. The water has become cold. Guest, go to the fire! -- Your fire is warm. -- Sit here and warm yourself. -- May the gods give you good things.
uncertain: ghr.so read as 2SG middle imperative 'warm yourself'

english: What are you doing early? -- I am milking the cows. My daughter milks the sheep. -- Do the cows love you? -- They love me. We go home in the evening; I will sing. -- Sing for me. -- Sit and listen.
uncertain: kleuse not recognised; read as an imperative 'listen' (expected kludhi)

english: Did you hear the wind in the night? -- I heard it. The wind blew and the tree shook. The horses were afraid. -- Are they still afraid now? -- They are not afraid. The wind has stopped.
uncertain: kle:m as 1SG aorist of klew- unexpected (expected kleum)
leytt read as 'has ceased/gone away', root not certain

english: Do your dogs guard the sheep? -- By night and by day, and they keep watch. My dog is not afraid. -- Does it kill wolves? -- Last year it killed a she-wolf. -- It is a dear dog.
uncertain: dedwoye read as perfect of dwey- 'fear'
h1ey kewos kwo: h1ey read as interjection or 'it'
